audit.whatIsWrong: The page says "Thunderclap (E) armour-shred" in spikes[0].text, early and wants.foe[2], and refers to "his E shred" in mid and late. It also calls Unstoppable Force a "point-and-click knock-up" in two fields while calling it an "Un-dodgeable dash" in three others — and simultaneously tells you to dodge it.
audit.why: Thunderclap is his W, and it creates aftershocks on his attacks — no shred. The E is Ground Slam, which "deals magic damage based on his Armor and reduces the Attack Speed of enemies". Nothing in his kit reduces your armour. And Riot's R text is "launches himself to a location at high speed" — a location charge, so it can be sidestepped, which is why the dodge advice was right and the 'un-dodgeable' label wrong.
audit.corrected: Ground Slam named as the E with its attack-speed cut, Thunderclap restored to the W as an auto reset, and the ultimate described consistently as a 130s charge to a location in all five fields.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction in this lane was absent: Ground Slam's attack-speed reduction against Spirit Cleave.
audit.why: Yone's W text: "Spirit Cleave's cooldown and cast time scale with attack speed." Ground Slam reduces attack speed on a 7s cooldown — so his E does not just lower your DPS, it lengthens your shield's cooldown and slows the cast. That is why extended trades inside Ground Slam range go badly.
audit.corrected: Stated in report[5].t, breakdown.cooldowns, tradeBad and spikes[0].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 2 was Skill against whys[1] ("his shield and E shred keep short trades in his favour"), Levels 4-5 were Yone against whys[3] ("even out"), and Level 6 was Malphite against whys[4] ("stays even").
audit.why: Packet chart reads Malphite, Malphite, Yone, Skill, Skill, Yone, Yone — matching the whys on all three rows.
audit.corrected: Row 1 to Malphite, rows 3 and 4 to Skill on BOTH layers as one group, with the phase whys rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown for Unstoppable Force appeared anywhere despite the whole page being built around baiting it.
audit.why: 130/115/100s against Fate Sealed's 120/100/80s — his ultimate is longer than yours at every rank, which is what makes baiting it worth a whole lane phase.
audit.corrected: 130s written into phases[4].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, spikes[1].text and late.

notes: Two slots were swapped on this page: Thunderclap is the W (an auto reset with aftershocks), Ground Slam is the E — and neither shreds armour. Ground Slam reduces ATTACK SPEED, which matters more than the page realised because Spirit Cleave's cooldown and cast time scale with attack speed; that interaction is now stated. The page also called the ultimate 'un-dodgeable' in three fields while telling you to dodge it in two others; Riot's text (a charge to a location) settles it. NOT written to the page: the kit's derived grounding flags on Seismic Shard and Ground Slam — Riot's text for neither ability mentions grounding, and if it were real it would deny your Q3 dash, so it needs confirming before it goes near a live page.
